title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational workflows for: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging pipeline and retention, data residency and retention, secure software development lifecycle (SDLC), incident response security procedures, compliance evidence collection, and handling of risk exceptions. It is intended for control owners, engineers implementing controls, product managers, and auditors.

Owners and Scope
- Document owner: Security team (Aisha Patel)
- Primary stakeholders: Eng-sre, Eng-platform, Eng-infra, Product, Legal & Compliance
- Applies to: Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment control planes, and security-sensitive operational tooling.

1) RBAC & Authentication Model
Purpose: Enforce least-privilege access across control plane, infra, and internal tooling.

High-level model:
- Identity provider: Okta (SCIM provisioning + group sync).
- Roles: platform-admin, infra-admin, svc-account, eng, eng-readonly, se, security-analyst, support.
- Groups: role groups are authoritative; do not assign roles directly to users.
- Service accounts: scoped to a single service; long-lived keys restricted; require rotation and justification.

Role and permission conventions:
- Use coarse-grained roles mapped to fine-grained policy templates in IAM (e.g., AWS IAM, GCP IAM, internal authz).
- Role naming: team-role-environment (e.g., infra-admin-prod).
- Time-limited elevation (JIT): Vault/OIDC-based short-lived role elevation for admin tasks via Just-In-Time access. Session duration default = 1 hour, max = 8 hours (requires manager approval).
- MFA: Enforced for all human accounts for any privileged role (hardware key preferred).
- Passwords & SSO: Enforce SSO only; password auth disabled for internal apps when possible.

Operational rules and checks:
1. Account provisioning: use HR-triggered Okta provisioning; owner assigns groups.
2. Quarterly access review: Role owners must review and attest to membership.
3. Service account review: review every 90 days; document purpose and owner in the service-account registry.
4. Approval matrix: Any change to platform-admin or infra-admin requires 2 approvers from security or infra leads.

Examples (policy snippet, textual):
- platform-admin: create/update service configs, run rollouts, manage dedicated capacity.
- infra-admin-prod: manage cloud accounts, network, infra scaling.

2) Audit Logging: Capture, Pipeline, Detection, and Retention
Goals: Ensure tamper-evident, searchable, and retained audit evidence for administrative and data access actions. Support forensic and compliance requests.

What we log:
- Authentication events: login successes/failures, MFA events, token creations/refreshes.
- Administrative actions: role changes, policy updates, canary/rollout launches, model pushes.
- Data access: customer data reads/writes (as applicable), export requests, deletion requests.
- System events: node lifecycle, autoscaler activity, KV cache flushes (metadata only).
- Service-to-service auth: service token usage (token id, scope, timestamp).

Log pipeline (implementation overview):
- Agents: Fluentd/Vector on hosts or sidecars collects structured JSON logs.
- Transport: TLS -> central collector -> Kafka for buffering.
- Storage: Cold storage S3 (encrypted), warm store in Datadog/Splunk/Elastic for 90 days.
- SIEM & detection: Datadog Security Signals + Splunk correlation searches + PagerDuty alerts for high-severity findings.

Retention and access:
- Admin & change logs (critical): 7 years (S3 Glacier Deep Archive for >1 year).
- Authentication logs: 2 years for compliance-critical accounts; 1 year for general auth logs.
- Application API access logs: 90 days in warm store; 1 year in cold archive.
- Backup logs & exports: 7 years (audit requirement).

Retention table (textual):
- Log type: Admin/Config changes | Warm retention: 90 days | Cold retention: 7 years
- Log type: Auth/Audit events | Warm retention: 90 days | Cold retention: 2 years
- Log type: API access | Warm retention: 90 days | Cold retention: 1 year

Integrity and tamper-evidence:
- S3 objects are write-once; bucket versioning + MFA delete enabled for the audit buckets.
- Logs are hashed (SHA-256) and periodic signed manifests are generated weekly.
- Access to raw audit buckets is RBAC-protected and requires approval from Security and Infra.

Search and alert SLAs:
- Alerting latency: 95% of critical alerts surface within 60s of ingestion; 99% within 2 minutes.
- Forensics visibility: 99.9% of admin events available in SIEM within 2 minutes of occurrence.

Query examples (text):
- S3 retrieval: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-prod/2026/02/14/admin-log-2026-02-14.json.gz ./
- Splunk example search: index=audit sourcetype=okta action="group.user.add" | stats count by user, group

3) Data Residency & Retention Controls
Principles: Customer-configurable residency; data separation for private/dedicated; strong encryption and predictable retention/deletion semantics.

Residency model:
- Account property: each customer account has a region tag (e.g., us-west-2, eu-central-1).
- Host routing: requests for a resident account are routed to the matching data region by the control plane policy layer.
- Private/on-prem: data remains on customer-managed network when deployed private.

Encryption & key management:
- At rest: AES-256 for object storage, envelope encryption using cloud KMS.
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites; mTLS between internal services.
- BYOK: Supported for Dedicated and Private; KMS keys mapped to account resources.

Retention & deletion workflows:
- Default retention: customer application logs and user-generated artifacts 90 days in warm store.
- Customer deletion request process:
  1) Customer opens deletion request via Console/Support ticket.
  2) Support verifies identity and scope; Security & Legal notified for regulated customers.
  3) Deletion job runs: removes records from primary DB, object store, and asynchronous caches.
  4) Backups & snapshots: scheduled purge cycle ensures removal from backups within defined SLA (30–90 days depending on backup tier).
  5) Final attestation: system generates a deletion certificate stored in evidence repo.

Backup retention defaults:
- Live DB snapshots: 30 days
- Long-term backups (S3): 90 days
- Archived backups for regulated customers: up to 7 years (per contract)

Data residency exceptions and approvals: Any exception to store customer data in a non-resident region requires documented approval from Security + Legal and an updated risk assessment.

4) Secure Software Development Lifecycle (Secure SDLC)
Goals: Shift-left security; reduce vulnerabilities in production by integrating security into each stage of development.

Controls by phase:
- Design: Threat modeling required for services that handle customer data or privileged control plane operations. Owner: Engineering lead + Security reviewer.
- Build: Dependency scanning (Snyk/OSS scan) on every PR; enforce vulnerability severity blocking rules (critical & high must be fixed or have approved exception).
- Test: SAST in CI, DAST for public endpoints on release candidate; fuzzing for core runtime components.
- Release: Security checklist gating release; SBOM generated and attached to every release.
- Operate: Runtime secrets rotation, runtime anomaly detection, and periodic pentests.

CI/CD security gates (examples):
- PRs affecting infra-config.yaml must pass infra-lint, SAST, and a security-approval label before merge.
- Merged PRs trigger automated canary for 2% of traffic for 1 hour with rollback automation on errors > 5% or latency regressions > 30%.

Secrets and artifacts:
- Secrets: stored in Vault with ACLs; no secrets in source control. Pre-merge scans block secrets if detected.
- Artifacts: signed and stored in private registries; images scanned for runtime vulnerabilities.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures
Alignment: This security incident response procedure integrates with the company-wide incident process documented in oncall-and-incident-response.

Classification and initial triage:
- Severity levels: Security-S1 (critical data exfiltration, production control-plane compromise), Security-S2 (privilege escalation, config leak), Security-S3 (vulnerability disclosed without evidence of exploit).
- Pagering: S1 escalates to Security Incident Lead + CTO + Legal + Engineering oncall; S2 escalates to Security Lead + Eng SRE.

Immediate actions (first 60 minutes):
1) Contain: isolate affected service(s), revoke any suspected compromised tokens or keys, apply network ACLs as needed.
2) Preserve evidence: snapshot affected hosts, preserve logs and network captures to an evidence bucket (write-once).
3) Notify stakeholders: internal comms channel (#sec-incidents), PagerDuty, Legal & Compliance, designated account owners for customer-impacting incidents.

Forensic and remediation steps:
- Forensic imaging and analysis: Security & Forensics contractor (if engaged) performs forensic analysis.
- Root cause analysis: within 72 hours include timeline, attack vector, impacted data, and mitigations.
- Customer notification: follow Legal templates; targeted notification within regulatory SLA (e.g., GDPR: 72 hours for personal data breaches when required).
- Post-incident: full IR retrospective and evidence package for auditors; schedule a remediation and verification plan.

Communication templates (text):
- Initial internal alert: "Security Incident detected: [summary]. Status: investigating. Impact: [systems/customers]. Next updates: every 60 minutes."
- Customer notification (if required): pre-approved legal template with contact, timeline, and mitigation steps.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows (SOC2, ISO27001, Contractual Audits)
Purpose: Provide a repeatable, auditable process for gathering, maintaining, and producing evidence for auditors.

Evidence repository and ownership:
- Source: Evidence stored in the Evidence Repo (S3 bucket + indexed catalog).
- Evidence types: policies, runbooks, system screenshots, config exports, access attestation logs, pentest reports, vendor contracts.
- Control owners: every control has a designated owner listed in the Control Matrix.

Periodic tasks:
- Quarterly evidence refresh: control owners update attestation artifacts and mark as current.
- Annual readiness review: security leads prepare binder for auditors and perform gap remediation.

Audit request process (steps):
1) Request received by Security via email or shared ticket queue.
2) Security maps requested controls to evidence artifacts using the Control Matrix.
3) Export evidence bundle from Evidence Repo, redact where needed, and provide via secure share.
4) If evidence missing: log as finding, assign owner, and track to closure with target date.

Common evidence examples (text):
- RBAC: group membership export from Okta with attestation timestamp.
- Audit logging: signed weekly manifest + sample admin log for representative period.
- Backups: snapshot listing and retention policy export.

7) Risk Register and Exceptions Process
Principles: Risks are tracked, mitigated, or accepted with documented compensating controls. Exceptions are time-boxed and require explicit approval.

Exception request process (steps):
1) Submit exception form (Confluence form link) including: control, justification, compensating controls, risk level, duration requested, and owner.
2) Security performs risk assessment and recommends mitigations.
3) Approval: For low risk, Security Lead can approve; for medium-high, Security + Legal + impacted platform owner approval required. High-risk exceptions require CTO or CISO sign-off.
4) Exception monitoring: create a ticket with reminders at 30-day intervals; automatic expiry and re-evaluation required.

Example exception (text):
- "Service account SVC-legacy requires long-lived credentials for a legacy integration. Requested duration: 6 months. Compensating controls: IP allowlist, additional monitoring rule, quarterly attestation." Status: Approved (Security Lead) until 2026-08-01.

Risk register items to track (textual):
- Data residency mismatch for customers with conflicting legal requirements
- Third-party vendor dependency on single provider for log aggregation
- Legacy service accounts with elevated privileges

C. Control matrix excerpt (text):
- Control: RBAC membership reviews | Owner: IAM Team | Evidence: Okta group export + attestation
- Control: Admin action logging | Owner: Platform Team | Evidence: signed weekly manifest + sample logs
- Control: Backup retention | Owner: Infra | Evidence: backup policy export + snapshot listing

D. Glossary (short):
- JIT: Just-In-Time access
- BYOK: Bring Your Own Key
- SIEM: Security Information and Event Management
